dossier.public_summary: The dip is V-shaped, 14% deep and shows a 60% odd-even difference, signalling an eclipsing binary at 2.6 days on the target itself. The implied size is stellar (~23 Earth radii plus phase curve) and the star's astrometry indicates binarity. The signal is on the target, so it is a stellar companion, not a planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even eclipses differ by 160 sigma for this 1.3 d period; even eclipses are 1.6x deeper. This is positive evidence for a binary at twice the period (2.6 d), not a planet, seen in 5/5 sectors with same sign (sector_oe_same_sign_share=1, sector_oe_max_sigma=93.58).
Extremely V-shaped (v_sigma 85) with short ingress favours grazing stellar eclipse over flat-bottomed planet transit; fit_b=0.6297 and star_density_penalty=14320 also mismatch planet density.

Dilution-corrected depth gives 22.7 R_earth (28.8 R_earth with Gaia FLAME radius) – well above 22 R_earth star threshold. Stellar RUWE=2.281 and excess_noise_sig=37.21 support the target itself is an eclipsing binary.

Significant out-of-eclipse modulation ~2% of dip depth indicates ellipsoidal/reflected light, not a planet. Centroid is on_target and neighbours could not cause it (could_cause_within_1px=0, plausible_within_1px=0). sector_depths_by_source and stellar_radius confirm no planet-like consistency.
